speaker: narrator
text: Chapter 1: Snow at the west stair. Irval Monastery clung to the mountain as if stone could pray harder than flesh. Its walls rose from black cliffs, its roofs bent under May snow, and its bell tower leaned over a ravine where clouds collected like wool torn from a giant spindle. At dusk the monastery showed one light only, a dull amber point in the scriptorium where Nima Darel, apprentice illuminator and unwilling keeper of errands, trimmed a lamp that smelled of soot and bitter resin.

speaker: narrator
text: The monks called that lamp ordinary because no one wished to say its older name after sunset. Visitors called it the Ashen Lantern, a bronze bowl blackened by some forgotten fire, set with mica panes that turned every flame gray. It was supposed to be kept empty in the Hall of Vows. That evening it burned on Nima's desk without oil, wick, or permission.

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "Brother Tovan, do not tell me a draft did this," Nima said, holding her steadying knife above the page. "A draft scatters gold leaf. A draft makes the saints look cross-eyed. It does not climb three locked corridors, settle in my lamp stand, and light a relic the prior keeps behind two keys and a sermon."

speaker: Tovan Aric
text: "I will not blame the wind unless it presents symptoms," Tovan Aric replied. The physician-monk stood in the scriptorium door with snow melting from his hood and ash-gray herb stains on his cuffs. "Set down the knife, Lamp Hand. If the relic chose your table, it may have chosen a witness, not a victim."

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "Bell moved," Ysolde Fen said from behind him. The bell keeper had come barefoot from the tower, a coil of hemp rope over one shoulder and frost on her braid. "No pull. One shiver. Wrong hour."

speaker: narrator
text: Nima looked from Brother Ash to Ysolde, then past them to Garron Vey, the courier crouched near the brazier pretending to warm his hands instead of counting exits. Kell Rusk, the cook, filled the rear of the room with steam from a covered pot. Behind Kell waited a veiled pilgrim in a lacquer mask, and behind the pilgrim stood Savitri Morn, the visiting magistrate, who had arrived that afternoon with a writ and no patience for mountain weather.

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "If the bell is taking exercise by itself, may I recommend we all encourage its independence from a lower valley?" Garron said. "I have carried letters through three bandit roads, one goat stampede, and a tax clerk's birthday feast, and none of them began with furniture lighting itself."

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "For the record," Savitri Morn said, opening a leather notebook already spotted with snow, "state who first observed the lantern burning, who had legal custody of it, and whether any person present has touched it since the flame appeared."

speaker: Kell Rusk
text: "Take one holy lamp, two keys, a pinch of prior's temper, and seven witnesses too hungry to lie well," Kell said. "That is how the kitchen would write the recipe. If you want the rumor version, add that Brother Leth saw gray light walking under the chapel door before supper."

speaker: Amaya Sol
text: "My name is Mara-of-the-Stair tonight," the masked pilgrim said softly. "I touched nothing. I saw the glow under the scriptorium sill while Cook Rusk was telling Garron that cold beans are a form of penance. If names matter, I can give you a second one tomorrow."

speaker: monastery bell
text: Inscription on the outer rim of the great bell: COUNT THE BREATHS BETWEEN TOLL AND ECHO. A TRUE VOW RETURNS WHOLE. A FALSE VOW COMES BACK AS ASH.

speaker: narrator
text: The lantern burned lower when the inscription was read aloud, though no one admitted noticing until later. Its gray flame bent toward the west stair, the narrow passage leading down to the sealed Hall of Vows, where Prior Caldus kept the monastery charters, the penitents' tokens, and a cedar coffer that Nima had never seen open. The prior himself had not appeared for vespers.

speaker: narrator
text: Chapter 2: The Hall of Vows. Savitri ordered no one to move the lantern, then ordered everyone to move with her. That contradiction did not trouble her; she made Tovan carry the relic in an iron ash pan, made Ysolde walk behind him to watch his hands, made Nima bring wax tablets, and made Garron carry the magistrate's satchel because panic, she said, should be usefully employed.

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "Magistrate Morn, Brother Ash, Ysolde, Garron, Cook Rusk, and Mara-of-the-Stair can all swear I have only the scriptorium key," Nima said as they passed the icon of Saint Oris. "The prior kept the vow key. Master Pel kept the pigment stores. If the lamp left the Hall, someone borrowed a path I do not know."

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "You will answer the question asked, Apprentice Darel," Savitri said. "When did you last see Prior Caldus alive, and did he address you as Nima Darel, Lamp Hand, child, copyist, or by any term suggesting private confidence?"

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "He called me Lamp Hand at noon and child at dusk," Nima answered. "At noon he said my vermilion was too bright for a martyr's blood. At dusk he sent me away from the Hall because Brother Orvek, the steward, had brought accounts. He never used my family name unless he was angry, and he was always angry when accounts were mentioned."

speaker: Tovan Aric
text: "Caldus complained of chest tightness after supper," Tovan said. "I gave him hawthorn, not sleep tincture. He refused examination. He had ink on his right thumb, lampblack beneath two nails, and the sour breath of a man who had been fasting to make other people feel guilty."

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "He rang none," Ysolde said. "Prior rang for everything. Tea. Pen. Forgiveness. Today, none."

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "I delivered a packet to him at first bell," Garron said, then swallowed when Savitri's pen stopped. "Small packet. Red seal. Not poison unless poison now pays courier rates and demands dry wrapping. He told me to wait for a reply. I have been waiting so long my boots have developed legal opinions."

speaker: Kell Rusk
text: "The scullions said Brother Orvek carried a sealed ledger like a roast that needed hiding from dogs," Kell said. "Add chopped fear, simmer under a steward's sleeve, and serve with excuses. I am not accusing him, Magistrate. I am seasoning the room."

speaker: Amaya Sol
text: "Stewards are useful masks," Amaya said from behind her lacquer face. "Pilgrims learn that at shrines. A steward says no, and pilgrims think the saint refused them. A prior says yes, and the steward decides which door yes must use."

speaker: narrator
text: The west stair tightened as it descended. Candles guttered in shallow wall niches. Names of dead abbots had been carved on each landing, but the newer carvings were crowded and uncertain, as if the chisel had hesitated. At the lowest turn, the Ashen Lantern flared without heat, and every shadow on the stair leaned upward toward the living.

speaker: monastery bell
text: Tolling record carved beside the west stair: ONE FOR DAWN, TWO FOR BREAD, THREE FOR BURIAL, FOUR FOR FIRE, FIVE FOR A SOUL UNNAMED, SIX FOR AN OATH BROKEN, SEVEN FOR THE DOOR THAT OPENS INWARD.

speaker: narrator
text: The Hall of Vows stood open. Its cedar door had not been forced. Snow had blown through a slit window and made a pale crescent on the floor, but no boot marks crossed it. Prior Caldus lay beside the coffer, face turned toward the wall, mouth dark with soot. His right hand clutched a strip of vellum on which one unfinished word had dried: Sol.

speaker: narrator
text: Chapter 3: Statements in the refectory. Savitri moved the living away from the dead because bodies, she said, have the patience of evidence and witnesses do not. Dawn came late behind storm clouds. The refectory smelled of barley, wet wool, old smoke, and the sharp spirits Tovan used to clean his instruments. Brother Orvek, the steward, had locked himself in the accounts cell and claimed prayer through a novice.

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "I will hear each statement in the presence of the others," Savitri said. "Contradiction is more useful when it occurs while faces are visible. Brother Aric, begin with the condition of the deceased. Do not offer theology unless theology left bruising."

speaker: Tovan Aric
text: "Prior Caldus died before the bell shivered," Tovan said. "His lips show soot, but his throat does not. The soot was placed after death, perhaps with a cloth or thumb. There is bruising at the left wrist, a puncture near the collar, and a bitter almond scent under the hawthorn. That scent did not come from my remedy."

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "Poison," Ysolde said. "Then theater."

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "Splendid, we have theater on a mountain with no audience but snow," Garron said. "If anyone asks, I prefer comedy. In comedy the courier survives, marries someone with a bakery, and never again sleeps under a bell that mutters like an uncle with debts."

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "Courier Vey," Savitri said, "state the origin of the red-sealed packet, the person who paid you, and the precise words, if any, spoken when it changed hands."

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "A woman in Grayhook paid me," Garron said. "Old cloak, new gloves, voice like she had swallowed a pin. She said, 'To Prior Caldus at Irval, by his own seal, and tell the Lamp Hand that ash remembers shape.' I thought Lamp Hand was a title for whoever cleans chimneys. That shows the quality of my education."

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "Ash remembers shape," Nima repeated. "That is from a binder's charm. My first master used to say it when scraped parchment took ink again. Brother Pel said the charm belonged to Serra Sol, the illuminator who burned the west archive thirty years ago. He said she died nameless. He said many things when he wanted apprentices frightened."

speaker: Amaya Sol
text: "Your Brother Pel lied with an old man's economy," Amaya said. "Serra Sol did not die nameless. Some names are buried by men who fear daughters will learn to read grave markers."

speaker: Kell Rusk
text: "There it is," Kell said, spreading his hands. "Take one dead prior, fold in a daughter, sprinkle thirty-year ash, and every monk at breakfast remembers urgent chores. The novices already whisper that Serra's ghost knocked over the salt. I told them ghosts prefer pepper because it travels farther."

speaker: narrator
text: Several monks crossed themselves when Kell mentioned Serra Sol. Nima watched Amaya's mask instead. The pilgrim did not turn toward the corpse room, the storm windows, or the steward's locked cell. She watched the Ashen Lantern, which sat unlit on the refectory table and still managed to darken the wood beneath it.

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "Mask knows lamp," Ysolde said. "Lamp knows name. Prior knew both."

speaker: Amaya Sol
text: "Bell keeper," Amaya replied, "some doors open because a key turns. Some open because everyone in the room finally admits the wall was only painted. I came as Mara-of-the-Stair. I may leave as Liora Venn. Neither name is the one your prior feared."

speaker: narrator
text: Chapter 4: The scriptorium under seal. Savitri sealed the Hall of Vows with red wax and made Ysolde stand guard because no one sane would try to argue past the bell keeper twice. Then she took Nima, Tovan, Garron, Kell, and Amaya back to the scriptorium. If the prior's last mark named Sol, the magistrate reasoned, the illuminated records might show why.

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "These folios are not arranged as I left them," Nima said. "The blue psalter was under weight. The tithe register was in the dry chest. The martyr leaf had no silver line through the throat. Someone has been reading like a thief who learned manners from a goat."

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "As the only professional carrier of other people's secrets present, I object to goats receiving blame for amateur work," Garron said. "A goat would eat the incriminating vellum. A human leaves it just visible enough for everyone to step closer and die of curiosity."

speaker: Tovan Aric
text: "Do not touch the silver line," Tovan said. "It is not silver. It is powdered moonseed mixed with gum. In sufficient amount it slows the breath, clouds the sight, and leaves a puncture blamed on a pin. Caldus handled a poisoned page before he died."

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "Apprentice Darel, identify who had the training to prepare such pigment," Savitri said. "Include illuminators, physicians, cooks with access to bitter seeds, and any pilgrim who has represented herself under more than one name."

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "I could grind it, but I would not mistake it for silver," Nima said. "Brother Pel could. Tovan could identify the plant but not lay a clean line with a squirrel brush. Kell owns knives, not patience. Amaya's hands are gloved. Garron could poison a man only by reading him one of his jokes at length."

speaker: Kell Rusk
text: "Moonseed in gum, that is a wicked sauce," Kell said. "The old kitchen rule says bitter kills where sweet carries it. Brother Orvek asked for honey cakes after nones, and Prior Caldus sent them back untouched. The scullions said Orvek looked relieved, which is not how a man receives rejected pastry unless pastry had a second office."

speaker: Amaya Sol
text: "Brother Orvek was steward when Serra Sol was judged," Amaya said. "He kept the witness list. He kept the keys. He kept his post when everyone else from that year became a plaque, a stain, or a lesson for apprentices."

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "Orvek hates bells," Ysolde said from the doorway, though no one had heard her arrive. "Pays boys to ring. Says rope blisters. Hands soft."

speaker: narrator
text: Savitri wrote that down. Nima noticed the magistrate had three columns in her book: fact, claim, pressure. The fact column was narrow, the claim column crowded, and the pressure column held only names. Caldus. Orvek. Serra Sol. Ashen Lantern. Beside the lantern's name, Savitri had drawn a small square and shaded it black.

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "We will now distinguish accusation from sequence," Savitri said. "A thirty-year scandal may provide motive. It does not explain how a dead man crossed clean snow, how the relic moved, or why a bell shivered without a pull."

speaker: monastery bell
text: Hidden lettering beneath old polish on the bell's throat: WHEN THE ROPE IS CUT, LISTEN TO THE HAMMER. WHEN THE HAMMER IS STILL, LISTEN TO THE HAND THAT FEARS A COUNT.

speaker: narrator
text: Chapter 5: Kitchen rumors. The storm closed the mule path by midday, leaving the magistrate with law but no road. Snow pressed against the shutters in wet slabs. In the kitchen, Kell fed everyone because hunger makes witnesses theatrical and because, as he told the novices, even murder must wait for broth if it expects clear answers. Nima sat near the flour bins, trying not to stare at Amaya's mask.

speaker: Kell Rusk
text: "Here is how the monastery cooks a secret," Kell said. "First, take a prior who says silence is humility. Add a steward who keeps keys under his pillow. Stir in a dead illuminator named Serra until the broth turns black. Then feed the result to children and call it history."

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "Cook Rusk," Savitri said, "you will separate kitchen metaphor from admissible memory. Did you personally see Brother Orvek handle the Ashen Lantern, the red-sealed packet, the honey cakes, or any key belonging to Prior Caldus?"

speaker: Kell Rusk
text: "Personally, I saw Orvek at the pantry hatch with the honey cakes," Kell said. "He said the prior required sweetness after fasting. I said fasting men snap at sweetness. He said the prior had changed. That was the wrong spice. Men change their sandals, Magistrate. They do not change their hatred of honey in one afternoon."

speaker: Tovan Aric
text: "Caldus avoided honey because of an old fever that left his throat swelling," Tovan said. "Anyone who served it to him either did not know him or knew him well enough to use the offer as a message. He would refuse the cakes, touch the note beneath, and perhaps prick himself on a prepared pin."

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "I am beginning to miss simple bandits," Garron said. "Bandits say, 'Give me the purse.' They do not say, 'Kindly refuse this pastry so a holy murder can proceed through stationery.'"

speaker: Amaya Sol
text: "Simple bandits rarely write histories," Amaya said. "Brother Orvek did. He wrote that Serra Sol stole the Ashen Lantern and fired the west archive to conceal it. He wrote that her infant died in winter. He wrote that no surviving kin could dispute the sentence. A steward's hand can be heavier than an axe."

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "You are that infant," Nima said. "Or you want us to think so. Mara-of-the-Stair, Liora Venn, pilgrim, daughter, witness - how many names must one person carry before any of them becomes evidence?"

speaker: Amaya Sol
text: "As many as men throw away," Amaya answered. "My mother gave me Amaya before they took her. A washerwoman gave me Liora when the hospice wanted records. I gave myself Mara when I climbed this mountain, because stairs ask less than gates."

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "Amaya Sol," Ysolde said. "Name fits vellum. Prior wrote Sol. Dead hand not subtle."

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "The court will not accept inheritance by poetry," Savitri said. "But it may accept a living claimant, a forged judgment, and a chain of custody if we locate documents older than Brother Orvek's accounts. Where would Serra Sol hide a truth in a monastery built to burn paper and worship memory?"

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "In pigment," Nima said. "Or under it. Illuminators scrape, size, gild, and cover. A page can carry two pictures if the first is patient. The Ashen Lantern's mica panes make gray light. Gray light reveals carbon differently than candle flame. If Serra hid testimony, she hid it where only that lamp could read."

speaker: monastery bell
text: Six dull taps traveled through the kitchen beams though the tower rope hung under Ysolde's hand. The old brothers crossed themselves. The novices counted wrongly. In the pause after the sixth tap, the bell seemed to hold back a seventh for someone not yet named.

speaker: narrator
text: Chapter 6: Gray light. Savitri returned the Ashen Lantern to Nima because investigation sometimes requires the suspect's skill. That choice made Brother Pel mutter, made Garron step farther from the table, and made Amaya straighten as if an invisible hook had lifted her mask. The lamp lit when Nima breathed across the empty cup. Its flame was gray, small, and utterly without warmth.

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "Do not crowd me," Nima said. "Gold hates breath, vellum hates damp, and I hate being watched by a magistrate, a doctor, a bell keeper, a courier, a cook, and a masked woman who may own the page before I finish proving it was stolen."

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "For fairness, I am watching the door, not you," Garron said. "The door has been honest so far. It remains closed, looks sturdy, and has not accused me of delivering murder parcels. I find this refreshing."

speaker: Tovan Aric
text: "Nima needs silence," Tovan said. "And a basin of clean snow, vinegar, three linen strips, and the thinnest knife from Kell's belt. If the hidden writing used lampblack, heat may damage it. If it used iron gall, vinegar will wake it like a fever."

speaker: Kell Rusk
text: "My thinnest knife is for onions, confessions, and cutting burnt edges off saints," Kell said. "Use it gently. The blade has heard more kitchen truth than the chapter house and deserves a better death than legal scraping."

speaker: narrator
text: Under gray light the martyr leaf changed. The painted saint's cloak thinned into smoke. Beneath the red folds appeared a second hand, smaller and fiercer than the official script. Nima read dates, names, payments, and a line of accusation written backward so that only the mica lantern, held at an angle, cast it right on the polished bone ruler.

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "Serra wrote that the archive fire began after Orvek locked the west cabinets," Nima said. "She says Prior Caldus was then only Brother Caldus and helped carry charred ledgers to the ravine. She says the Ashen Lantern was not stolen. It was used to read accounts hidden under devotional images. She names Orvek, Caldus, and Abbot Renn."

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "Read the next line exactly," Savitri said. "Do not soften grammar for the dead. Exact words carry jurisdiction."

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "If I die under censure, let my daughter Amaya inherit my name, my lamp, and the debt owed by Irval," Nima read. "Let whoever holds this lantern count the bell at false vespers. Orvek cannot bear a complete count."

speaker: Amaya Sol
text: "She remembered me," Amaya said. Her voice did not break; it narrowed. "All these years I wore borrowed faces because I thought my first name had no witness. She put it under a saint's cloak and trusted ash to outlive judges."

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "False vespers," Ysolde said. "Tonight. Storm muffles road. Orvek will move."

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "Then we will let him believe movement remains possible," Savitri said. "No accusation leaves this room. Brother Ash, you will continue examining poison. Cook Rusk, you will overfeed the monks. Courier Vey, you will look frightened in public, which I gather requires no rehearsal."

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "Magistrate, my terror is an artisanal craft," Garron said. "I have refined it across provinces. If Brother Orvek needs to see a man who appears both guilty and available for stabbing, I can be convincing from several angles."

speaker: narrator
text: Chapter 7: The tower count. Night settled early, weighted by storm. Ysolde led Nima and Garron up the bell tower while Savitri questioned monks below and Tovan arranged bottles in the infirmary where curious men might notice them. The tower stairs were colder than the outer yard. Each step held a shallow cup of ice. Above, the great bell waited in a timber cage blackened by old smoke.

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "Step where I step," Ysolde said. "Wood remembers fools. Garron, less breathing. Nima, lamp low. Bell dislikes bright."

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "The bell dislikes bright, the wood remembers fools, and the mountain keeps trying to enter through my sleeves," Garron said. "If anyone here writes travel advice, may I suggest valleys. Valleys have mud, fleas, tax men, and the occasional inn. I now see these as luxury features."

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "Ysolde, when you said the bell moved without a pull, did you mean the mouth swung or the hammer struck?" Nima asked. "Savitri thinks sequence matters. Tovan thinks symptoms matter. I think whoever made the lamp burn also knew what kind of movement you would notice first."

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "Hammer," Ysolde said. "Mouth still. Rope slack. Sound small. Like tooth on cup."

speaker: narrator
text: They found the trick above the bell, not below it. A second cord, blackened with soot and thin as a lute string, ran through a pulley hidden behind a carved seraph. It did not swing the bell. It tugged the clapper just enough to make a private count. Beside the pulley, a smear of honey had frozen on the wood.

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "I respect a crime that brings its own dessert," Garron said, then backed into Nima when the floor creaked. "No, forgive me, I respect nothing. I renounce respect. I would like the record to show I was born for ground-level cowardice and have been tragically promoted."

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "Honey on the pulley would hold a hair or thread until the room warmed," Nima said. "When the kitchen fires climbed through the flue, the honey softened, the cord slipped, and the clapper tapped. Orvek could make a bell speak while dining below with witnesses."

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "Clever," Ysolde said. "Too clever. Hates bells, studies bell. Fear teaches."

speaker: monastery bell
text: On the inner lip where only a climber could read: SEVEN IS NOT A NUMBER. SEVEN IS THE WITNESS WHO STAYS WHEN SIX HAVE LIED.

speaker: narrator
text: The seventh tap came then, not from the hidden cord. The whole bell breathed it. Snow shook from the tower louvers. Down in the yard, someone crossed the white space between kitchen and accounts cell with a covered bundle under one arm. Even from above, with storm veiling the lanterns, Nima recognized Brother Orvek's careful, soft-handed walk.

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "That is our steward, yes?" Garron whispered. "Please say it is not a new murderer. I have organized my panic around one man and would hate to begin fresh paperwork."

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "Orvek," Ysolde said. "Bundle. Ravine path. Go."

speaker: narrator
text: Chapter 8: Brother Ash sets a snare. Tovan had not gone to the infirmary merely to arrange bottles. He had left the shutters unlatched, the lamp high, and the corpse report open on his desk with several deliberate mistakes. A guilty reader, he told Savitri later, often corrects what an innocent reader fears to touch. He also set out three cups: water, bitter tea, and a harmless tincture labeled moonseed.

speaker: Tovan Aric
text: "I expected Brother Orvek to look for what I knew," Tovan said. "Instead he looked for what I had misnamed. He moved the moonseed label from the harmless bottle to the bitter one, then wiped his fingers on his sleeve. That does not convict him of murder by itself. It convicts him of wishing the diagnosis to point elsewhere."

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "Did you witness this directly?" Savitri asked. "State your position in the room, the lighting, whether anyone else was present, and whether your own arrangement created an inducement a court might find improper."

speaker: Tovan Aric
text: "I stood behind the drying screen," Tovan said. "The light came from two tallow lamps and the snow glare. Brother Pel slept in the cot after too much grief and not enough soup. As for inducement, Magistrate, I placed labels on bottles. If Orvek found temptation in paper, that is a theological problem trying to become a legal one."

speaker: Kell Rusk
text: "Brother Ash baits traps like he salts stew," Kell said. "Not too much, just enough for the guilty tongue. Orvek came through the kitchen after, asked whether old vellum burns faster than new, and pretended he meant oven fuel. No cook likes a man who lies about firewood."

speaker: Amaya Sol
text: "He was measuring how quickly a page might disappear," Amaya said. "My mother's hidden leaf is not the only record. Caldus would not have kept thirty years of guilt in one saint's sleeve. Men like him bury truth in several graves so they can visit whichever one feels safest."

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "The cedar coffer was open when we found him," Nima said. "But the coffer smelled of juniper, not cedar, and the bottom plank sat too high. I noticed because apprentice hands clean what prior hands display. There is a false bottom. Orvek's bundle may be whatever Caldus hid there."

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "Then I vote we pursue the soft-handed steward with the suspicious parcel down the ravine path in a blizzard," Garron said. "I make this vote under protest, terror, and the faint hope that heroic couriers are paid extra by someone, someday, in a currency accepted at warm inns."

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "Your objection is noted and denied," Savitri said. "Ysolde will lead. Nima will carry the lantern. Tovan will bring antidotes and bandages. Cook Rusk will remain with the monks and prevent rumor from becoming riot. Amaya Sol will come because the bundle may concern her claim, and because if I forbid her, she will follow badly."

speaker: Amaya Sol
text: "I follow well," Amaya said. "I have followed rumors across hospice wards, river courts, shrine roads, and men's silences. But I accept your order, Magistrate Morn, because obedience is a useful disguise when everyone is watching rebellion."

speaker: monastery bell
text: Five taps rolled through the tower, then one, then one. The novices later argued whether the count was seven, a warning, or only loose metal in storm wind. Ysolde wrote a single word in the tower ledger: ANSWER.

speaker: narrator
text: Chapter 9: The ravine path. Irval's ravine path was less a road than an argument between mountain and gravity. It descended behind the bakehouse, crossed a shelf of black slate, then narrowed under ice-bearded pines before vanishing toward the old archive ruins. Orvek's lantern showed ahead as a yellow blot, not gray like the Ashen Lantern but ordinary and human and therefore, to Nima, more frightening.

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "Single file," Ysolde said. "No hero feet. Snow lies."

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "Snow lies, stewards poison, bells editorialize, and magistrates recruit couriers into alpine law," Garron said. "I am collecting regional customs. If I survive, I shall publish a pamphlet titled Places Not To Deliver Packets."

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "Courier Vey," Savitri said, "if you fall, scream before impact if possible. It will help establish distance. That is not encouragement to fall."

speaker: Tovan Aric
text: "No one is falling," Tovan said. "Put weight on the inside edge, breathe through the scarf, and do not grip the lantern arm if you stumble. Flame, law, and panic all travel poorly when dropped."

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "The gray flame is leaning toward the ruins," Nima said. "It did that on the west stair. It is not pointing to Orvek exactly. It is pointing to where the old archive burned. Amaya, if your mother hid more there, tell us now before the mountain decides to edit our choices."

speaker: Amaya Sol
text: "I know only one thing she wrote outside the leaf," Amaya said. "A woman who raised me had a scrap with Serra's mark and four words: ash under second water. I thought it meant a cistern. I searched three. Perhaps it meant snowmelt beneath ruins. Perhaps it meant I spent years being almost right, which is another kind of prison."

speaker: narrator
text: Orvek's light vanished near the broken arch of the west archive. The ruins had no roof, only ribs of charred stone and a floor buried under hardened drifts. Thirty years of weather had washed the walls clean of smoke, but the place still smelled faintly of old heat when the wind blew down from the tower.

speaker: Kell Rusk
text: "Back in the kitchen," Kell told the monks who tried to crowd the yard, "the recipe for staying alive begins with not chasing murder into weather. Add doors barred, broth hot, tongues occupied. Brother Pel, if you faint again, choose a bench. The floor has given enough testimony today."

speaker: narrator
text: Kell's voice did not reach the ravine, but his work did. No monks followed. No novice ran screaming after them with a half-heard accusation. For once rumor stayed in its pot. Savitri would later write that Cook Rusk had preserved public order through soup, insults, and the strategic distribution of stale rolls.

speaker: monastery bell
text: The bell did not toll while they crossed into the ruin. Snow absorbed the monastery behind them. In that muffled dark, the absence of sound felt written: A COUNT WITHHELD IS STILL A COUNT.

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "Fresh scrape," Ysolde said, kneeling by a fallen threshold. "Bundle dragged. Orvek hurried. Fear heavy."

speaker: narrator
text: Chapter 10: Second water. The phrase became clear only when Nima lifted the Ashen Lantern over the old baptismal font. The first water was gone, frozen and thawed away decades earlier. The second was stone: a shallow basin beneath the basin, hidden by a disk blackened to match the floor. Ysolde pried it up with her bell knife. Beneath lay oilcloth, bone tubes, and a ledger wrapped in a child's wool scarf.

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "This scarf is not thirty years old," Nima said. "The ledger may be Serra's, but someone opened this place after the fire. Caldus, maybe. Or Orvek. The cloth has the same juniper oil as the coffer. The prior moved records between hiding places and died before choosing which guilt to keep."

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "Do not open the ledger yet," Savitri said. "We will mark its condition, witnesses present, weather conditions, and location. Brother Aric, confirm whether the oilcloth bears recent handling. Ysolde Fen, observe the threshold. Courier Vey, stop making that face unless the face is evidence."

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "This is my evidence face," Garron said. "It records that I am cold, frightened, and standing in a burned shrine beside a hidden ledger while a murderer with better gloves is nearby. Future courts may find it persuasive."

speaker: Tovan Aric
text: "Recent handling," Tovan said. "The knot was retied by someone with a stiff left thumb. There is dried salve on the cloth, pine tar and calendula. I made such salve for Orvek's cracked nail three weeks ago. I remember because he complained that charity should smell less rustic."

speaker: Amaya Sol
text: "Open it," Amaya said. "No, forgive me. Mark it, measure it, ask the mountain to notarize it if you must. But my mother's scarf is in that hole, and every rule that slows your hand feels like one more monk telling me to wait outside a locked archive."

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "Amaya Sol, daughter of Serra Sol, your objection is recorded," Savitri said. "So is your standing. Law moves slowly because haste is where men like Orvek hide knives. I will not let his hurry govern your mother's proof."

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "Light," Ysolde said. "Behind arch. Yellow. Low."

speaker: narrator
text: Orvek had not fled far. He stood beyond the cracked apse with a storm lantern at his feet and the cedar coffer's false bottom tucked under one arm. He saw them see him. His face, usually soft with cultivated patience, pinched into the expression of a man who had spent thirty years counting exits and discovered the last one occupied by witnesses.

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "Brother Orvek," Garron called, voice lifting too brightly. "Lovely night for archival housekeeping. If you are out for a constitutional, I should mention the magistrate has brought several questions and I have brought enough cowardice to run for both of us."

speaker: Tovan Aric
text: "Do not approach him," Tovan said. "He has one shoulder high, right sleeve weighted, breath fast. A knife or vial. Orvek, if you can hear me, set down the coffer board and show both hands. There is no treatment for falling into that ravine except not doing it."

speaker: monastery bell
text: From the tower above, seven full tolls entered the storm. None was thin. None was delayed. Each came back from the ravine whole, as if the mountain itself had decided to count aloud.

speaker: narrator
text: Chapter 11: The steward's fall. Orvek did not answer. He stepped backward into blowing snow, then sideways, choosing the old service ledge that ran behind the apse. Ysolde moved first. She crossed the ruin with the efficient anger of a woman whose bell had been made to lie. Nima followed with the Ashen Lantern, and the gray flame lengthened toward Orvek's sleeve.

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "Stop," Ysolde said. "Ledge rotten. Snow lip false. Stop now."

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "Brother Orvek," Savitri called, "you are ordered in the name of the valley court to halt, preserve the object in your possession, and submit to questioning regarding the death of Prior Caldus, the concealment of records, and the falsification of monastic accounts."

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "She means stop," Garron added. "The rest is decoration with teeth."

speaker: narrator
text: Orvek drew a vial after all. He flung it at the Ashen Lantern, perhaps hoping oil would smother gray fire or poison would blind witnesses. Tovan knocked Nima's wrist down. The vial broke on stone, releasing a bitter green smell. Where drops struck snow, the crust collapsed into pinholes.

speaker: Tovan Aric
text: "Do not breathe close to it," Tovan said. "Moonseed steeped in spirits. Nima, wash your glove in snow and do not touch your face. Amaya, stay behind Savitri. Garron, if you must shake, shake away from the spill."

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "He tried to put out the lantern," Nima said. "Not kill me first. The proof frightened him more than living witnesses. Magistrate, the gray flame is showing writing on the coffer board. There are names under the varnish."

speaker: Amaya Sol
text: "Let them burn into him," Amaya said. "No, Brother Ash, do not look at me as if vengeance is a fever. I know it is. I have carried it long enough to describe the pulse. But let him see the names once before law takes him."

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "Law does not require mercy from the injured," Savitri said. "It requires custody of the accused. Ysolde, can you reach him without losing footing?"

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "Could," Ysolde said. "Shouldn't. Ledge cracked. He moves, it goes."

speaker: narrator
text: Orvek moved. The ledge broke exactly as Ysolde had said it would. For one suspended breath the steward hung by both hands from a root glazed with ice, the coffer board trapped between his chest and the cliff. Garron threw himself flat and caught Savitri's belt when she lunged; Tovan caught Garron's coat; Nima planted the Ashen Lantern in the snow and reached with both scraped hands.

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "I have you, Magistrate," Garron shouted. "Possibly. Briefly. With all the legal authority of a terrified deliveryman. Brother Orvek, if you survive, please note I helped save the person arresting you, which ought to reduce any future haunting."

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "Take my hand, Brother Orvek," Nima said. "Not because you deserve it. Because if you fall with that board, everyone you buried must wait again, and I am finished letting your fear choose the pace of truth."

speaker: narrator
text: Orvek took her hand. Then the coffer board slipped. Amaya caught it against her chest, lost her mask to the wind, and stood bare-faced in gray light while the painted names bloomed across the varnish: Serra Sol, Amaya Sol, Prior Caldus, Brother Orvek, Abbot Renn, three merchants, two judges, and a line that made Savitri inhale once through her teeth.

speaker: narrator
text: Chapter 12: Names under varnish. They returned to Irval before dawn with Orvek bound, the ledger wrapped, the coffer board guarded under Savitri's cloak, and Amaya's broken mask swinging from Garron's belt like a conquered beetle. No one spoke on the ravine path except Ysolde, who said ice twice and duck once. The monastery gates opened before they knocked.

speaker: Kell Rusk
text: "I kept the broth alive, the monks indoors, and Brother Pel from confessing to crimes committed before his birth," Kell said when they entered. "That last required pepper tea and threats. If anyone wants breakfast, the recipe is oats, shock, and enough salt to remind the body it remains employed."

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "Bring every monk above novice rank to the refectory," Savitri said. "Bring sealing wax, dry cloth, a clean table, and the tower ledger. Brother Orvek is to be watched by two persons who did not serve under him. Brother Ash, examine his hands before he remembers an illness."

speaker: Tovan Aric
text: "His left thumb is split where the pulley cord ran," Tovan said after a glance. "There is moonseed residue under the nail, honey on the cuff, pine tar salve at the cut, and fresh bruising where he gripped the ledge. He will claim frostbite before guilt. Frostbite has less imagination."

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "Rope cut from his store," Ysolde said. "Bell clean now. Angry, but clean."

speaker: Amaya Sol
text: "I want my mother's name read before his," Amaya said. "Not as victim only. As illuminator, witness, and creditor. Say Serra Sol first, Magistrate. The dead hear order even when courts pretend they do not."

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "The record will begin with Serra Sol," Savitri said. "It will then state that Amaya Sol, also known during travel as Liora Venn and Mara-of-the-Stair, presented a claim supported by concealed testimony, physical evidence, and living witnesses. It will not call survival deceit."

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "Then write that Nima Darel, called Lamp Hand by people who need errands, saw the hidden script under gray flame," Nima said. "Write that the apprentice who was told to copy saints found sinners under them. Write that Caldus tried too late, maybe, but still tried. I do not know what mercy does with that."

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "Write that Garron Vey, courier of excellent balance and limited courage, delivered the original packet without reading it, climbed a tower against medical advice, and held a magistrate's belt with admirable civic commitment," Garron said. "Also, if possible, write that he is owed hazard pay by every institution represented here."

speaker: Kell Rusk
text: "Hazard pay is a stew with no ingredients," Kell said. "But I can give you second breakfast. Take oats for survival, onions for courage, and a burnt crust for the steward, who will receive none because prisoners should learn that kitchens remember."

speaker: monastery bell
text: Dawn inscription, read after the seventh clean toll: ASH IS NOT THE END OF FIRE. ASH IS THE SHAPE FIRE LEAVES FOR HANDS WILLING TO READ.

speaker: narrator
text: The seventh toll faded into a morning so clear the lower valleys appeared one by one below Irval, green and distant and almost innocent. Snow slid from the roofs. Novices swept the west stair. Brother Pel wept over Serra's leaf and did not ask to be forgiven. Orvek sat silent under guard, soft hands bandaged, eyes fixed on the Ashen Lantern as if it might still be persuaded to forget.

speaker: narrator
text: Chapter 13: The magistrate's table. Savitri converted the refectory into a court because the road remained buried and delay favors those who own keys. She set Serra's ledger, the coffer board, the poisoned martyr leaf, the red-sealed packet, the pulley cord, and Tovan's mislabeled bottles in a line. Nima noticed that evidence looked smaller in daylight, but the spaces between objects looked larger, as if every absence had gained weight.

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "This inquiry will record findings for the valley court," Savitri said. "It will not pronounce final sentence. It will determine custody, preserve documents, and identify immediate danger. Any monk who mistakes rank for immunity may test that belief against my patience, which has been reduced by altitude."

speaker: Tovan Aric
text: "Prior Caldus was poisoned by contact with prepared moonseed and later marked with soot," Tovan said. "The soot was from the Ashen Lantern's old cup, not from the Hall fire. His hand wrote Sol after death had begun loosening the fingers. That suggests remorse, recognition, or an attempt to name his murderer by naming the wronged."

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "Caldus feared count," Ysolde said. "Orvek feared count more. Both heard seven."

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "The hidden script says Caldus helped bury Serra's testimony," Nima said. "But the later marginal signs are his. See the heavier pressure, the tremor at the curves. He copied Orvek's payments onto devotional leaves and hid them where the gray lamp could find them. He made himself witness after being accomplice."

speaker: Amaya Sol
text: "Do not polish him too bright," Amaya said. "A man who repents after thirty winters still leaves a child outside thirty doors. Let the record show he turned because fear aged, not because justice called sweetly through his window."

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "For what little the courier vote is worth, fear can carry a message eventually," Garron said. "I have delivered letters ten years late and watched people kiss the paper anyway. Of course, none of those letters had murdered anyone first, which complicates the metaphor and my breakfast."

speaker: Kell Rusk
text: "Repentance is like old beans," Kell said. "Soak long enough and they soften, but nobody should pretend they are fresh. Caldus may have softened. Orvek stayed a stone in the pot and cracked the teeth around him."

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "Brother Orvek refuses to answer," Savitri said. "His refusal is recorded. His injuries are recorded. His possession of concealed evidence is recorded. The monastery will surrender its accounts, keys, and private punishment rolls before sunset, or I will classify the entire house as an obstruction with a chapel attached."

speaker: narrator
text: That sentence traveled through the refectory faster than rumor and much cleaner. Monks who had spent the morning looking at the floor found reasons to stand. The steward's deputies produced key rings, ledgers, wax tablets, and one locked reliquary that contained no bone at all but twenty-seven letters from valley families asking why daughters sent to Irval as copyists had vanished from reply lists.

speaker: monastery bell
text: At noon the bell gave two ordinary tolls for bread. No hidden cord answered. No gray echo followed. Ysolde wrote in the tower ledger: BREAD MEANS BREAD AGAIN.

speaker: Amaya Sol
text: "Bread means bread," Amaya said when Nima told her. "That may be the kindest miracle Irval has managed. I do not know whether to laugh, sleep, or break every locked box left in this place."

speaker: narrator
text: Chapter 14: The Lamp Hand's page. The storm held them three more days. During that time Savitri took statements until her ink froze twice, Tovan treated Orvek without gentleness but without neglect, Kell fed a monastery that had lost its appetite for certainty, and Garron rewrote his delivery ledger to include a new fee category called mountains attempting legal murder. Amaya slept little. Nima slept less.

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "I keep thinking of the unfinished word," Nima said to Tovan in the scriptorium. "Sol. It is a name, a sun, a note sung alone. Caldus wrote only three letters and made us carry the rest. Is that confession or cowardice?"

speaker: Tovan Aric
text: "Often both," Tovan said. "The dying do not become clean because breath shortens. They become brief. Caldus spent his last strength on the word he could still bear. It does not absolve him. It does tell us where to press."

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "Brother Ash, you speak as if guilt were a bruise," Nima said. "Color, pressure, swelling, tenderness. What do you prescribe when the whole house is bruised and everyone insists the purple is tradition?"

speaker: Tovan Aric
text: "Air, light, drainage, and no more tight bandages," Tovan said. "Also soup, because Kell will accuse me of malpractice if I omit it. For you, Lamp Hand, I prescribe a page that is yours before anyone orders it copied."

speaker: narrator
text: So Nima began a new illumination on scraped vellum from the exposed account books. She painted no saint. She painted the Ashen Lantern on a table with seven shadows around it: a magistrate's pen, a physician's cup, a bell keeper's rope, a courier's boot, a cook's knife, a pilgrim's broken mask, and an apprentice's stained hand. Under gray wash she hid smaller figures: Serra writing, Amaya listening, Caldus turning too late, Orvek counting wrong.

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "Good page," Ysolde said when she saw it. "Too many words, maybe. Lamp right."

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "I admire any artwork in which my boot appears braver than the rest of me," Garron said. "If copies are made, please ensure the boot is shown pointing downhill toward safety. Posterity deserves accuracy."

speaker: Kell Rusk
text: "Paint a bowl too," Kell said. "Every mystery thinks it is solved by ledgers and lamps, but nobody confesses properly on an empty stomach. Add a bowl near the corner. Not large. I do not need glory. Just steam."

speaker: Amaya Sol
text: "Paint the mask broken," Amaya said. "Not discarded. Broken things can still testify to the shape forced on them. And paint my mother's name where no varnish can cover it unless someone scrapes through the page."

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "When that page is complete, I will attach a copy to the court packet as visual index," Savitri said. "Do not make that face, Apprentice Darel. Law is more willing to read beauty than it admits, provided beauty arrives with numbered exhibits."

speaker: monastery bell
text: Evening toll, third day after the death of Prior Caldus: four for fire, then seven for witness, then one for the hand that lights without burning.

speaker: narrator
text: Chapter 15: Descent. The road opened under a hard blue sky. Valley riders came with spare mules, chains for Orvek, and sealed boxes for the evidence. Savitri supervised each bundle. Tovan sent medicines for the descent. Kell packed bread until Garron accused him of trying to ballast the entire court. Ysolde watched the tower shadow move across the yard and said nothing for almost an hour, which made the novices nervous.

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "Custody passes to the valley court at the lower bridge," Savitri said. "Until then, Brother Orvek remains my prisoner, the evidence remains under my seal, and any appeal to monastic privilege will be answered by asking why monastic privilege required poison, pulleys, hidden ledgers, and a courier who has not stopped talking since Tuesday."

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "I can stop talking," Garron said. "I simply prefer witnesses to my continued existence. Silence sounds too much like snow deciding whether to collapse."

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "Talk keeps fear warm," Ysolde said. "Acceptable."

speaker: Amaya Sol
text: "I will go down with the ledger," Amaya said. "Not because courts heal anything quickly, but because my mother's name has spent enough years above the clouds. Valleys remember differently. They have markets, children, gossip, and graves with flowers instead of warnings."

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "Will you come back as Amaya?" Nima asked. "Or Liora Venn, or Mara-of-the-Stair, or some fourth name that lets Irval pretend it did not owe the first one?"

speaker: Amaya Sol
text: "I will come back as Amaya Sol if I come back," Amaya said. "But do not mistake a true name for an unmasked life. People earned my caution. I may keep the hood, the gloves, and three escape routes. Identity is not a door I leave open for convenience."

speaker: Tovan Aric
text: "That is sensible medicine," Tovan said. "A healed wound still dislikes careless fingers. Return or do not return by your own measure. Irval has taken enough choices from your family."

speaker: Kell Rusk
text: "Take bread for the road, Amaya Sol," Kell said. "One loaf for hunger, one for anger, one for the magistrate when law forgets to eat, and one for Garron so he can chew instead of composing his obituary aloud."

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "My obituary will be tasteful," Garron said. "Garron Vey, beloved by inns, misunderstood by mountains, survived by unpaid invoices and a mule who never appreciated his singing. Actually, that is too moving. I need a moment."

speaker: narrator
text: They laughed because the alternative was to listen to chains. Even Savitri allowed the corner of her mouth to move. Orvek did not look back at the tower. Brother Pel did, and so did half the monks, as if the bell might toll one more accusation after them. It did not. It waited for Ysolde's hand.

speaker: monastery bell
text: Departure inscription chalked by Ysolde beneath the tower ladder: NO HAND, NO TOLL. NO TRUTH, NO PEACE. RING CLEAN OR KEEP SILENT.

speaker: narrator
text: Chapter 16: The clean toll. After the riders left, Irval Monastery did not become pure. Stone keeps cold, and institutions keep habits longer than stone. But locks changed. The punishment rolls were read aloud and burned in the yard. Letters were sent to families who had been answered with silence. Brother Pel resigned the pigment keys. Nima Darel, still an apprentice because skill does not ripen in one murder, received custody of the Ashen Lantern under Ysolde's witness and Tovan's complaint that relics make poor patients.

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "I do not want to be keeper of a lamp that chooses inconvenient hours," Nima said. "I want pigments that behave, margins that stay measured, and saints whose eyes do not follow me like creditors. But if the alternative is Orvek's cupboard, give me the key."

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "Key given," Ysolde said. "Use. Hide nothing important. Hide chocolate if needed."

speaker: Kell Rusk
text: "For the record, bell keeper, the kitchen has no chocolate," Kell said. "If it did, I would hide it from magistrates, murderers, apprentices, doctors, pilgrims, couriers, and bells. Some secrets preserve civilization."

speaker: Tovan Aric
text: "Begin with the living records," Tovan said. "Names of current novices, medicines, injuries, letters owed. Mysteries breed where ordinary duties are neglected. The Ashen Lantern exposed murder because the house had already accepted smaller darkness as routine."

speaker: Nima Darel
text: "Then help me make a list," Nima said. "Ysolde for bells, Kell for kitchen stores, you for infirmary, Brother Pel for pigments until he can surrender them properly, and Garron by letter for outside deliveries. Savitri will ask formal questions even from the valley. Amaya will ask harder ones when she is ready."

speaker: Ysolde Fen
text: "Good," Ysolde said. "Seven witnesses. More if needed."

speaker: narrator
text: Nima's first official act was not grand. She opened the scriptorium shutters. Dust lifted in pale sheets. The mountain air entered with the smell of thawing pine and mule tracks. On the far table lay Serra Sol's copied testimony, Savitri's receipt, Tovan's poison report, Ysolde's tower count, Garron's invoice, Kell's grease-spotted witness note, and Amaya's single unsigned line: I was named before I was hidden.

speaker: Amaya Sol
text: "You asked whether names become evidence," Amaya had written before descending. "They do when someone risks speaking them, someone risks hearing them, and someone writes them where fire has to work hard. Keep the gray lamp, Lamp Hand. Make it lazy by giving it less darkness to read."

speaker: Garron Vey
text: "Postscript from the lower bridge," Garron's later letter said. "The magistrate refuses to authorize hazard pay but admits my belt-holding was timely. I consider this a partial victory. Also, Orvek hates mule travel. Please tell Ysolde the bell may add one toll for poetic justice."

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "Official addendum," Savitri wrote in the packet's final page, "the Irval matter demonstrates that alias, occupation, title, and relation may obscure but need not defeat identification when testimony is anchored to acts. The claimant Amaya Sol is recognized for purposes of restitution inquiry. The apprentice Nima Darel is commended for technical competence under pressure. The courier is denied hazard pay pending statutory review."

speaker: monastery bell
text: Final tolling formula entered in the renewed tower ledger: ONE FOR DAWN. TWO FOR BREAD. THREE FOR BURIAL. FOUR FOR FIRE. FIVE FOR THE NAME RETURNED. SIX FOR THE OATH BROKEN. SEVEN FOR THE WITNESS WHO STAYS.

speaker: narrator
text: When spring finally reached the monastery, the Ashen Lantern sat cold in its new niche beside Nima's desk. It did not burn for every lie. It did not correct every memory. It was only bronze, mica, ash, and a history of being used by hands both brave and frightened. Yet on evenings when the bell counted cleanly and the scriptorium windows held the valley's last light, Nima sometimes saw gray shine gather in the empty cup, waiting not to accuse, but to read.

speaker: Savitri Morn
text: "Do not write that as Morn's confession," Savitri Morn asked, while the bell keeper examined a bell toll counted by different hands and Kell repeated what Lamp Hand had supposedly heard near the herb infirmary. "I said lawful custody mattered; I did not say it belonged to me. In this monastery a title can be borrowed faster than a candle, and a borrowed title casts the wrong shadow when the lantern turns gray." The interruption forced Savitri's pen to stop halfway through a name.

speaker: narrator
text: At the kitchen court, Savitri Morn, Kell Rusk, and Nima Darel reached the same evidence from three different angles. Footprints ending at a wall made the room feel staged, though no one could agree who had arranged it. The danger in the moment was attribution: a warning overheard by one person, repeated by a second, and denied by a third could become three different truths before anyone had lied on purpose.
